homelessConcepts: Logging facade: none. Sinks are scattered: EditorWindow::m_Log (command line, Qt), SaveTrace (Core), UpdateService LogSilently (Network), StartupFailure startup-failure.log (Windows), and Qt qWarning/qDebug calls in src/qt. The final map must decide whether Core owns one facade or only the file sink.
Settings store: AppCommandState holds nearly all settings in one god struct. There is no Settings system. Core owns the value vocabulary; the holder and its consumers belong to the final map.
Duration and ETA text: FormatEtaRemaining is pure formatting used only by a progress UI. Core or UI?
Lat/long DMS label: FormatLatLongLabel and CadCommands_Geo FormatDms. Geo or Core formatting?
Plot-scale labels: PlotScaleChoicesFor and PlotScaleLabel (util/PlotScales.hpp) are Document or Plot, not Core.
Slope text: FormatSlope (CadCommands.cpp) is grading/Terrain.
Station text: FormatStation (Alignment) belongs to Alignment, not Core.

2D point and vector types: curveisect::Vec2 (curveintersect.hpp), Alignment Point2, geo Pt and TraverseCalc Point are all 2D points. Shx::Vec2 is font-unit geometry, not Math. The final map decides whether Math owns one 2D vector type.

2D affine transforms: Xf2 (LibreDwgCad.cpp), Affine2D (DxfIo.cpp), Xf (ConvertDrawing.cpp), PlotSheetTransform Transform, PdfAlign Transform and CadCommands Transform (grid rotation). Math could own one affine type, but each owner keeps its domain meaning (for example grid rotation is Survey).

Matrix representations: double row-major Mat4 (gltfimport.cpp) and float column-major out16 arrays (Camera::OrthoProjection, ViewportRenderer::Ortho). The final map must choose one representation or document why two exist.
Camera and projection matrix construction is pure math but Renderer owns it. ucs::PlanViewAngles also encodes the camera convention in Math. The final map decides which side owns that convention.
Degree wrapping: ucs::PlanViewAngles, AzimuthAboutWorldZDeg and SnapToPolarRay (wrap180) each carry their own wrap loop. A shared helper is a candidate once Math is moved.

PlotSheetTransform Transform, PdfAlign Transform and Pt, and the Math-owned Xf2/Affine2D/Xf sections together form a set of 2D affine and point types. Math should own one of each, and the owners keep their domain meaning.

Input event vocabulary and document/command-state change notifications: no toolkit-neutral Events files or dispatcher exist. Qt viewport handlers and callbacks currently carry the behavior (auditedEntries.Events and sections); the final map/move tickets must decide event payloads, subscription lifetime, and the source of document-change notifications.

Appearance vocabulary: src/ui/CadUiStyleWidgets.hpp holds the named colour palette, linetype names, and lineweight ladder. It is not UI-neutral: it includes CadEntities.hpp (Commands/Document). The final map must assign it to Document (entity appearance) or GoSurveyEditor.

Report text policy: GitHubIssueUrlForReport and SendOutcomeMessage (platform/FailureReportUi.cpp, declared in FailureReportUi.hpp) are pure text helpers beside a Windows dialog. Owner is Debug (crash reporting) or UI; the final map decides.

OS text clipboard: CopyUtf8TextToClipboard (platform/FailureReportUi.cpp) is the only engine-side OS clipboard call. Qt-side clipboard and timer use is in src/qt. The generic part belongs behind the UI clipboard interface; the Win32 calls stay Windows.
ETA text: FormatEtaRemaining is used only by progress UI; it is either Core formatting or UI presentation (see the entry above, now with its UI caller identified).

Dialog-open flags and dialog-wait phases in Commands state (CadCommands.hpp insertBlockDialogOpen 5601, wblockDialogOpen 5659; CadBlocks.cpp WaitDialog phases): the state is Commands-owned; the decision to open a dialog is GoSurveyEditor's. The final map should decide whether the pending-question state moves to a Commands-owned prompt type.

Pending-question prompt state: AppCommandState::PointEditPrompt and projectRefreshPrompt (CadCommands.hpp ~5441) and AnswerPointEdit (commands/ProjectWarnings.hpp:40). The header comment says the dialogs live in ui/CadUi_Projects.cpp, which does not exist in src/ui. Owner of the prompt state is Commands or Projects; the dialog is UI.
Start-screen thumbnail cache (platform/ThumbnailCache.hpp): disk cache of drawing thumbnails; owner is Document or the start-screen owner, not UI.
Map-capture status text: CadOnlineMap.cpp:348 formats "Capturing map... N of M" into mapCapture.prompt. Commands should emit values (gathered, total); the string belongs to UI presentation.
Point-edit prompt raising: RaisePointEditPrompt (commands/ProjectPoints.cpp:118-269) and the pointEditPrompt state. Commands owns the question; the dialog is UI.
couplings: Foot/meter conversion constants are duplicated in several systems: geo/DrawingConversion.cpp, io/LandXmlIo.cpp, pdf/PdfMeasure.cpp, traverse/JobXmlImport.cpp, traverse/TraverseCalc.cpp, traverse/TraverseLeastSquares.cpp (kMetersToFeet), traverse/StarNetImport.cpp. Core units should own them.

Commands includes ray3d.hpp (2 files), ucs.hpp (3 files) and OrthoConstrain.hpp (1 file) directly, but the draft map does not list Math among Commands' allowed dependencies. Once these files are mapped to Math, each include counts as a violation. The final map must add Math to Commands or move the includes.
RotateFrameInPlace is duplicated with identical bodies in brep.cpp:2433 and AcisSatParser.cpp:541.

The 2D rotation-about-base helper is copied at least 6 times: RotateAroundBase (CadCommands.cpp:10623), RotatePtForAnnotationPreview (:24425), RotateSurveyCoords (SurveyPoints.cpp:361), RotatePdfInsertAroundBase (EditorViewport.cpp:101), Xf2::apply and Xf::P (IO and ConvertDrawing), and Affine2D. Replace callers with one Math helper; do not move code in this audit.
ucs::PlanViewAngles mirrors Camera's stored orientation by measurement, not by a shared derivation. Renderer may depend on Math, so the camera should call the Math function rather than repeat it.

ucs::OrthographicPresets holds UI display names (Top, Front) and is consumed by the View-tab combo and the ViewCube. ucs::AzimuthAboutWorldZDeg feeds the ViewCube compass. Math owns the frames; the labels and widgets belong to UI and Qt.
ucs::SnapToPolarRay is generic angle quantisation. Whether POLAR applies is Interaction policy, and its gating lives in Commands.
ray3d::RayTriangleIntersect is pure Math, but its documented contract (project onto the analytic surface) is a Geometry concern. Its comment cites brep faces.
OrthoConstrain.hpp implements ORTHO (REQ-047). The mode and when it applies are Interaction. Only the lock math is Math.

The 2D reflection helpers are also duplicated: ReflectPtAcrossLine and ReflectAngleAcrossLine (CadCommands.cpp:10638, :10655), and ReflectSurveyCoords (SurveyPoints.cpp:373), repeat the reflect math written inline at CadCommands.cpp:1566. Replace callers with one Math helper; do not move code in this audit.
Duplicate rotation: brep.cpp RotateAbout (6425) is the same Rodrigues formula as ray3d::RotateVectorAboutAxis. Replace with the Math function.

Angle-wrap helpers are repeated in six places with three different ranges: WrapPi in (-pi, pi] (TraverseLeastSquares.cpp:33), Wrap2Pi in [0, 2pi) (curveintersect.cpp:16), NormalizeTwoPi in (0, 2pi] (HatchBoundary.hpp:33), NormalizeAngleRadMinusPiToPi (CadCommands.cpp:10718), SweepBetween (brep.cpp:16343), and Core NormalizeAngle360 (Core.cpp:16, Core-owned, see auditedEntries.Math.pendingAssignment). Math should own one helper per range, and the callers should pick by range.
The 2D cross product is repeated: curveisect Cross (curveintersect.cpp:12) and brep Cross2v (brep.cpp:16302). brep also has Dot2, Mul2 and Len2 (16300-16303), which duplicate the same primitives.
The 2D rotate-and-scale affine is repeated in geo LocalGridTransform (LocalToGrid, GridToLocal) and in the Math-owned Xf2, Affine2D and Xf sections. One Math 2D affine would serve all of them.
TraverseCalc.cpp repeats the polar-to-rectangular step (slopeDist * sin / cos of an angle) at lines 113-120, 470-471 and 552-553. A generic polar-to-rectangular helper is a candidate for Math.
MirrorFrameInPlace (brep.cpp:2551) mirrors the same frame fields that RotateFrameInPlace (brep.cpp:2433, AcisSatParser.cpp:541) rotates. The frame transforms should live together in Math.

Qt input transport is coupled directly to command and interaction state: EditorViewport receives Qt mouse/key/wheel events, reads and mutates AppCommandState, and calls Commands/Interaction helpers. Events can own neutral event data and dispatch, but the adapter and behavior must be separated during the move.

Viewport change notification is a raw std::function<void()> (EditorViewport::changed), wired in EditorWindow to ResetDraftingInput() and Refresh(). The callback conflates command-state changes, repaint/refresh, and input reset; a future Events interface must distinguish those causes without taking ownership of UI refresh policy.

Document dirty tracking is revision polling, not a change event: EditorWindow compares m_State.cadGpuRevision with m_State.activeDocSavedRevision for the active drawing, and documents[i].cadGpuRevision with documents[i].savedRevision for other tabs; BCLOSE compares cadGpuRevision with blockEditCleanRevision. These counters are Commands/Document-owned and no DocumentChangedEvent publisher contract exists yet.

Qt event handlers invoke command and interaction policy directly, including CadClassifyRightClick/CadRightClickHoldIsMenu, snapping, selection, command submission, and viewport navigation. The Events boundary should transport intent only; these policies stay with Commands/Interaction/Renderer.

AdjustmentWindow::drawingChanged is the current explicit adjustment commit-attempt notification: after its guards, CommitToDrawing emits before the count==0 check, including no-op attempts, and EditorWindow subscribes only to refresh. It is a Qt callback, not a toolkit-neutral publisher; the final map must connect it to a Document-owned change source or an Events adapter.

The viewport changed callback is invoked from mouse/key handlers and also from grip-menu actions, map-capture status polling, selection-box cancellation, and the timed right-click callback (all emission sites are recorded in sections). One no-argument callback currently conflates command/interaction state changes and refresh-only updates.

The app-wide Qt input route is split between EditorWindow::eventFilter and EditorWindow::DraftingInputEvent in EditorInput.cpp; they intercept keys, shortcut overrides, mouse presses, text entry, undo/cancel, and command submission. Events can own neutral input transport, while Qt focus routing and Commands own policy.

The Events input boundary in this audit means app-level input routed into command/interaction state. Widget-local event callbacks remain with Qt or the domain widget (for example PdfCanvas to PdfWindow); those callbacks use Qt types and implement local presentation or PDF gesture policy rather than a shared event contract.

EditorWindow::CloseDrawing (EditorWindow.cpp:2501-2527) and closeEvent (EditorWindow.cpp:2529-2560) orchestrate Qt window/tab closure with GoSurveyEditor SwitchDrawing/save flow, Qt ConfirmSave, Document dirty state/documents and drawing-tab erasure, Renderer viewport geometry invalidation, Commands ProjectsWithUnsavedPoints/CancelActiveCommand/RestoreDocumentFromSnapshot/FlushProjectPointDb, IO gsproj::Release, Qt settings persistence, and the Network installer path. The code lives in src/qt, so this is app-level workflow inside the Qt adapter layer, not a toolkit-neutral Events publisher.

Exclusion rule for remaining Qt event overrides: widget-local resizeEvent/showEvent/changeEvent and closeEvent delivery stays with Qt; any application workflow inside a closeEvent is recorded separately under its owning application/domain systems. Only application-wide input routing or cross-system state-change notifications are assigned to Events.

Swept and not assigned to Events: EditorWindow::closeEvent (src/qt/EditorWindow.cpp:2529-2560). Qt delivers the request. The handler ignores close if a child refuses (2531), ConfirmSave is canceled (2535), or ProjectsWithUnsavedPoints refuses (2537-2542). The installer path is gated by m_UpdateExitPending (2550), not by m_LaunchInstaller being set. If LaunchInstallerAndExit returns false, the handler clears the pending flag, normalizes the phase only when it is still UpdateReady, restores drawing presentation, and ignores the close (2550-2558); an update launch failure can leave the phase Failed. It accepts the close when no update exit is pending or the launch succeeds. GoSurveyEditor coordinates child/tab/save workflow; Commands owns ProjectsWithUnsavedPoints; QSettings geometry/state persistence is Qt. LaunchInstallerAndExit starts the Network/update installer path but does not itself exit the process.

Swept and not assigned to Events: AdjustmentWindow::closeEvent in src/qt/AdjustmentWindow.cpp. Qt delivers the close request; the method applies a busy guard and runs ConfirmDiscard for the adjustment document workflow.

Swept and not assigned to Events: EditorWindow::nativeEvent (src/qt/EditorChrome.cpp:128-225). Qt invokes this GoSurveyEditor window adapter for Windows messages. On WM_COPYDATA, invalid payloads set *result=FALSE and return true (152-153); valid payloads queue a lambda that shows/raises/activates the window and calls OpenDrawing(path), set *result=TRUE, and return true (148-150). Native hit-test/minmax and WM_NCCALCSIZE use Win32 message handling. WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE/WM_EXITSIZEMOVE call EditorWindow::BeginInteractiveResize/EndInteractiveResize, which invoke EditorViewport resize-preview operations rather than Win32 APIs. Windows supplies the OS/IPC contract; this app-level external-open ingress is OS-specific and not a toolkit-neutral Events publisher.
